  # trace_filter

  Returns the call traces and rewards that match an address filter, from an inclusive block range or from one block selected by hash. Records are ordered by block, then transaction, then preorder, with each block's rewards after its transaction records. The trace\_\* notes describe ranges, matching, pagination and resource limits.

  Returns localized traces matching an address filter.

  ## Parameters (by position)

  **Filter** `object` *required*

  An explicit null member is the same as an omitted one. Callers use the member names exactly as defined; a server may match them case-insensitively, but every member takes effect as the member it matches or is rejected (-32602 recommended), never ignored, so an unknown member is rejected. Resolve tags once per request. Capture one coherent snapshot for the request; numeric and tag ranges select its canonical blocks. Validate selectors before count 0 returns \[]. OR within each address list; AND between lists by default, as eth_getLogs composes topic positions. Missing, null or empty lists are unrestricted. mode union matches either populated list instead. Compare address bytes independently of hex letter case. Match CALL sender/recipient, CREATE creator/created address and SELFDESTRUCT executing (self-destructing) account/beneficiary; after EIP-6780 that account usually survives. A record matches only addresses it reports; a failed CREATE reports no created address, so it has no created-address match. A reward matches toAddress by author and has no from side; in intersection mode it is excluded whenever fromAddress is populated, while in union mode a toAddress match suffices. Return an error rather than silently truncate when a server limit is exceeded.

      * **blockHash** `string or null`

        Selects exactly one block by hash, as in eth_getLogs (EIP-234); callers may omit it and clients implement it. A non-null blockHash is mutually exclusive with non-null fromBlock and toBlock (-32602 recommended); null is omitted. The result, including \[], is for that block, and each record carries its hash; address matching, mode, ordering and after/count apply as for a single-block range. The block must be canonical and executed; an unknown, noncanonical, unexecuted or otherwise unavailable hash returns an error (-32001; 4444 recommended for pruned history), never \[] or another block's records. Resolve the hash and trace the block in one chain view, never substituting a block by height.

      * **fromBlock** `string or string or null`

        Inclusive block range bound. The filter defaults omitted fromBlock and toBlock to the same latest head, so historical searches must explicitly set fromBlock. Bounds are numbers and the earliest, latest, safe and finalized tags; pending, block-hash strings and block-hash objects are rejected (-32602 recommended); numeric bounds fit uint64. Unresolvable safe or finalized tags return an error, never head substitution or an empty result. If either bound resolves beyond the current head block, or fromBlock resolves above toBlock, return an error (-32602 recommended); an explicit toBlock before an omitted latest start is such a reversed range. Never clamp the range or return a partial result. earliest is the lowest available block; never replace an explicit endpoint with a retention boundary, and return an error (4444 recommended) if required history is unavailable.

  ## Result

  **Result** `array<object> or array<object> or array<object> or array<object> or array<object> or array<object> or array<object> or array<object>`

      #### `Successful CALL` fields

      Array result. Each item independently matches one of the following variants; different variants may occur in the same array.

      **Result** `array<object>`

      Preorder traversal. The transaction and every CALL-family or CREATE-family operation that targets an account outside the precompile set emit a frame, whether they succeed, revert or halt. Retain root precompile calls regardless of value. Omit nested precompile frames with zero value, including one whose call fails its precheck; retain nested frames with nonzero transferred or inherited value, whether successful or failed. A precompile is an address in the precompile set active at the executing block's fork. traceAddress gives child ordinals and subtraces counts direct children in the emitted tree, excluding omitted frames. Omitting a call frame must not omit its caller VM return-memory effects. Any other CALL-family call that fails its precheck (call depth limit or insufficient balance) emits a frame with its action and error, a null result and no subtraces; the forwarded gas returns to the caller. A CREATE or CREATE2 that fails its precheck (call depth limit, insufficient balance or nonce overflow) emits the same kind of frame before Amsterdam; from Amsterdam the check runs in the creating opcode and no frame is emitted. A CREATE whose address collides emits a create frame with error "Contract address collision" that consumes its gas. Standalone historical records require localization; only protocol rewards have null transaction fields. Frames inside simulation and replay envelopes omit localization and protocol rewards. error alone determines failure. A REVERT frame has error "Reverted" and a required result \{gasUsed, output} carrying its revert bytes, for CREATE too, without address or code: no contract exists at the would-be address. An exceptional halt consumes the frame's action gas; its result is null. Failure labels are "Reverted", "Out of gas", "Bad instruction", "Bad jump destination", "Stack underflow", "Out of stack", "Mutable Call In Static Context", "Built-in failed" and "Out of bounds". As in Parity and OpenEthereum, a code-deposit failure, including code above the EIP-170 size limit, is "Out of gas", and returned code starting with 0xEF (EIP-3541) is "Invalid code". Beyond Parity, which reported an address collision as "Out of gas" and emitted no frame for a failed precheck, use "Contract address collision", "Nonce overflow", "Insufficient balance for transfer" and "Max call depth exceeded". EIP-3860 oversized initcode aborts the creating frame with "Out of gas". The designated invalid instruction 0xFE is an undefined opcode, so its frame fails with "Bad instruction". Clients may report other error strings, which consumers treat as a generic failure. revertReason is not defined by this specification; raw revert bytes live in result.output. Suicide and reward records carry result null. A suicide frame records the SELFDESTRUCT opcode and its transfer, not account deletion.

      Successful frame; result is required and error must be absent.

          #### `Result` fields

          * **blockHash** `string` *required*

            32 byte hex value

            *Match pattern:* `^0x[0-9a-f]{64}$`

          * **blockNumber** `integer` *required*

            Range: `>= 0`

            ***

          * **action** `object` *required*

            CALL and STATICCALL: from is the caller, to the target. DELEGATECALL and CALLCODE: from is the executing address, to the code address. value is the transferred value; DELEGATECALL reports the inherited value and STATICCALL 0. Root gas is the transaction gas minus intrinsic gas, including access-list and authorization costs. Nested gas is the gas forwarded after the EIP-150 63/64 cap, plus the 2300 stipend for a value transfer.

                #### `action` fields

      <summary>
        Show Option 2 `Reverted CALL` array
      </summary>

      #### `Reverted CALL` fields

      Array result. Each item independently matches one of the following variants; different variants may occur in the same array.

      **Result** `array<object>`

      Preorder traversal. The transaction and every CALL-family or CREATE-family operation that targets an account outside the precompile set emit a frame, whether they succeed, revert or halt. Retain root precompile calls regardless of value. Omit nested precompile frames with zero value, including one whose call fails its precheck; retain nested frames with nonzero transferred or inherited value, whether successful or failed. A precompile is an address in the precompile set active at the executing block's fork. traceAddress gives child ordinals and subtraces counts direct children in the emitted tree, excluding omitted frames. Omitting a call frame must not omit its caller VM return-memory effects. Any other CALL-family call that fails its precheck (call depth limit or insufficient balance) emits a frame with its action and error, a null result and no subtraces; the forwarded gas returns to the caller. A CREATE or CREATE2 that fails its precheck (call depth limit, insufficient balance or nonce overflow) emits the same kind of frame before Amsterdam; from Amsterdam the check runs in the creating opcode and no frame is emitted. A CREATE whose address collides emits a create frame with error "Contract address collision" that consumes its gas. Standalone historical records require localization; only protocol rewards have null transaction fields. Frames inside simulation and replay envelopes omit localization and protocol rewards. error alone determines failure. A REVERT frame has error "Reverted" and a required result \{gasUsed, output} carrying its revert bytes, for CREATE too, without address or code: no contract exists at the would-be address. An exceptional halt consumes the frame's action gas; its result is null. Failure labels are "Reverted", "Out of gas", "Bad instruction", "Bad jump destination", "Stack underflow", "Out of stack", "Mutable Call In Static Context", "Built-in failed" and "Out of bounds". As in Parity and OpenEthereum, a code-deposit failure, including code above the EIP-170 size limit, is "Out of gas", and returned code starting with 0xEF (EIP-3541) is "Invalid code". Beyond Parity, which reported an address collision as "Out of gas" and emitted no frame for a failed precheck, use "Contract address collision", "Nonce overflow", "Insufficient balance for transfer" and "Max call depth exceeded". EIP-3860 oversized initcode aborts the creating frame with "Out of gas". The designated invalid instruction 0xFE is an undefined opcode, so its frame fails with "Bad instruction". Clients may report other error strings, which consumers treat as a generic failure. revertReason is not defined by this specification; raw revert bytes live in result.output. Suicide and reward records carry result null. A suicide frame records the SELFDESTRUCT opcode and its transfer, not account deletion.

      REVERT; result carries the frame's gas and revert bytes.

  <div>
    <details>
      <summary>
        Show Option 6 `Halted CREATE` array
      </summary>

      #### `Halted CREATE` fields

      Array result. Each item independently matches one of the following variants; different variants may occur in the same array.

      **Result** `array<object>`

      Preorder traversal. The transaction and every CALL-family or CREATE-family operation that targets an account outside the precompile set emit a frame, whether they succeed, revert or halt. Retain root precompile calls regardless of value. Omit nested precompile frames with zero value, including one whose call fails its precheck; retain nested frames with nonzero transferred or inherited value, whether successful or failed. A precompile is an address in the precompile set active at the executing block's fork. traceAddress gives child ordinals and subtraces counts direct children in the emitted tree, excluding omitted frames. Omitting a call frame must not omit its caller VM return-memory effects. Any other CALL-family call that fails its precheck (call depth limit or insufficient balance) emits a frame with its action and error, a null result and no subtraces; the forwarded gas returns to the caller. A CREATE or CREATE2 that fails its precheck (call depth limit, insufficient balance or nonce overflow) emits the same kind of frame before Amsterdam; from Amsterdam the check runs in the creating opcode and no frame is emitted. A CREATE whose address collides emits a create frame with error "Contract address collision" that consumes its gas. Standalone historical records require localization; only protocol rewards have null transaction fields. Frames inside simulation and replay envelopes omit localization and protocol rewards. error alone determines failure. A REVERT frame has error "Reverted" and a required result \{gasUsed, output} carrying its revert bytes, for CREATE too, without address or code: no contract exists at the would-be address. An exceptional halt consumes the frame's action gas; its result is null. Failure labels are "Reverted", "Out of gas", "Bad instruction", "Bad jump destination", "Stack underflow", "Out of stack", "Mutable Call In Static Context", "Built-in failed" and "Out of bounds". As in Parity and OpenEthereum, a code-deposit failure, including code above the EIP-170 size limit, is "Out of gas", and returned code starting with 0xEF (EIP-3541) is "Invalid code". Beyond Parity, which reported an address collision as "Out of gas" and emitted no frame for a failed precheck, use "Contract address collision", "Nonce overflow", "Insufficient balance for transfer" and "Max call depth exceeded". EIP-3860 oversized initcode aborts the creating frame with "Out of gas". The designated invalid instruction 0xFE is an undefined opcode, so its frame fails with "Bad instruction". Clients may report other error strings, which consumers treat as a generic failure. revertReason is not defined by this specification; raw revert bytes live in result.output. Suicide and reward records carry result null. A suicide frame records the SELFDESTRUCT opcode and its transfer, not account deletion.

      Exceptional halt, including an address collision; result is null.
